summary: Feature successfully restores intended behavior for both recall grouping and multi-pass retrieval. Recall now properly excludes passive observations from default searches while allowing explicit scope='passive' queries. Multi-pass retrieval includes broad query compaction that reduces token usage when queries are over-dispersed across many files. All 49 relevant tests pass.

issues.description: Recall fix (3ab8987) reverted the earlier approach from 17524e6 which always searched with includePassive=true and filtered during display. The current approach (includePassive=scope==='passive') is simpler but loses the ability to show passive count in summary when not displaying them. The test expectations are consistent with this approach.

The compactBroadPackedNodes function only triggers when: intent='broad', tokenBudget>=8000, and currentTokensUsed > tokenBudget*0.5 (BROAD_EFFICIENCY_UTILIZATION_CAP). Queries with tokenBudget<8000 will not benefit from compaction even if over-dispersed. This appears intentional based on the constants chosen.

Broad compaction targets 48% utilization (BROAD_EFFICIENCY_TARGET_UTILIZATION=0.48) which is conservative. The compaction only removes high-level compression (levels 1-3) from nodes, preserving pivot symbols. This is appropriate for maintaining query relevance while reducing noise.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Feature commits 17524e6 and 3ab8987 represent a two-step fix: first the grouping logic was corrected in recall.ts, then the compaction defaults were restored in generator.ts. The later commit also adjusted recall to use simpler includePassive=scope==='passive' logic.
